text:
Carmen G.: Kicking off POC with MercuryPay. Goal: ingest streaming txns -> call an FX tool to attach rate + ttl -> return structured JSON per txn. Environment: VPC with SAML SSO, 30d retention. Asks: 1) Python asyncio streaming + function_call sample, 2) mapping of function/tool output to SDK events (how to consume structured JSON), 3) two pricing options (hosted on-demand + 3mo reserved for 500 qps), timeline ~3w.

Theo R.: Quick confirmations: egress allowed but they need IP allowlist. They prefer customer-managed KMS (HSM preference) but will confirm.

Nina V.: Python asyncio example (minimal) showing stream + function call handling:
```py
import asyncio
from redwood import RedwoodClient

async def run():
    client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${RW_KEY}")
    stream = await client.responses.stream(
        model="redwood-infer-prod-v1",
        input="Enrich txn with USD->EUR rate",
        stream=True,
        functions=[{
            "name": "fx_lookup",
            "parameters": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "pair": {"type": "string"},
                    "rate": {"type": "number"},
                    "ttl": {"type": "integer"}
                },
                "required": ["pair","rate"]
            }
        }],
        function_call="auto"
    )

    async for evt in stream:
        if evt["type"] == "function_call":
            # payload is structured JSON string
            data = evt["payload"]
            # parse and attach to txn
            print("TOOL ->", data)
        elif evt["type"] == "delta":
            print(evt["chunk"], end="")
        elif evt["type"] == "end":
            print("--stream end--")

asyncio.run(run())
```

Nina V.: Notes: SDK yields discrete events: delta (partial text), function_call (structured tool output as JSON string), end. We strongly recommend providing an explicit JSON schema in functions.parameters to prevent extra fields/hallucinations.

Theo R.: Routing + fallback behavior: you can prefer Reserved (Dedicated) and fallback to hosted-compatible model. Fallback preserves function_call plumbing but be aware of KMS differences when falling back. Example routing rule (console YAML):
```yaml
routes:
  - name: mercurypay-pref
n    prefer: dedicated
    match: customer_id == "mercurypay"
  - name: mercurypay-fallback
    prefer: hosted
    fallback: true
```

Carmen G.: Good. What about token limits for predictable latency?

Nina V.: For that family of models keep prompt+context <= 1k tokens to hit p95 targets on Dedicated. If longer history is necessary, use prefix/KV caching on the SDK to avoid re-sending tokens each call.

PricingBot: Hosted on-demand example: $0.022 per 1k tokens -> 1M tokens ≈ $22/mo. For sustained 500 qps peaks recommend 3mo reserved; estimated starting commit ~$8,500/mo (depends on model, latency SLO). HSM/Private add ~15-25% uplift. Expedited onboarding (2-week) is a one-time $2,000 fee.

SecBot: Uploaded security packet + SAML attribute mapping template: https://redwood.internal/sec/mercurypay/packet_499551.pdf. IP allowlist template: https://redwood.internal/onboarding/ip-allowlist-template.md

Theo R.: Engineering gotchas to call out in kickoff: 1) If fx_lookup needs external HTTP calls from Private, ensure NAT or an internal adaptor; 2) Ensure function JSON schema includes ttl/rate types to avoid casting surprises downstream; 3) Test fallback parity between reserved and hosted models with a short eval set.

Carmen G.: Action items: 1) I'll request IDP metadata + confirm HSM decision + egress CIDRs from customer (48h). 2) @PricingBot please produce hosted vs 3mo reserved slide + expedited line. 3) @Nina V. can you prepare a tiny demo harness that simulates 500 qps for 60s showing fallback behavior?

Nina V.: Yep, I'll prepare the harness and a short run RW-POC-9133. Will include a tiny JSON schema and an example of parsing the function payload into our ingestion pipeline.

PricingBot: I'll post the two-option quote here in ~2 business hours.
